course.title: MSSP: SOC 2 + ISO 27001 Engagement
course.audience: Run a real client engagement — SOC 2 + ISO 27001 compliance as an MSSP analyst.
course.description: A full client engagement: scope the work, assess the gaps, implement and test controls, then assemble the audit evidence package. Three roles, mapped to SOC 2 and ISO/IEC 27001.

roles.name: Offensive Security (Red)
roles.mission: Penetration testing and control validation for the client.
roles.label: 🎯 Offensive Security

roles.name: Managed Detection & Response (Blue)
roles.mission: Hardening, detection engineering, and incident response.
roles.label: 🛡️ Managed Detection & Response

roles.name: GRC / vCISO
roles.mission: Scope, risk, controls, and audit evidence — the compliance spine.
roles.label: 📋 GRC / vCISO

weeks.title: Onboarding & Scoping
weeks.objective: Sign the engagement and define the system / ISMS scope.
weeks.milestone: The engagement letter is signed and the system / ISMS boundary is written down and agreed.

weeks.title: Gap Assessment
weeks.objective: Assess current state vs SOC 2 + ISO 27001 and pick the controls.
weeks.milestone: Every SOC 2 and ISO 27001 requirement is marked met or gap, and the SoA names the selected controls.

weeks.title: Control Implementation
weeks.objective: Stand up the missing controls and write the control matrix.
weeks.milestone: Each gap has a control in place, and the matrix says which requirement it satisfies and who owns it.

weeks.title: Validation & Testing
weeks.objective: Pentest, detect, and evidence that the controls operate.
weeks.milestone: Testing is complete and every control has evidence that it actually operates, not just that it exists.

weeks.title: Audit Readiness
weeks.objective: Internal audit and assemble the evidence package (Type I / Stage 1).
weeks.milestone: The Type I readiness package is assembled and the client has the findings report.

gates.title: Scope & SoA signed
gates.description: The engagement agreement is signed and the Statement of Applicability defines which controls are in scope. Nothing is implemented before this.

handoffs.label: GRC → Blue: which controls to implement
GRC → Red: what may be tested

gates.title: Controls implemented
gates.description: Every applicable control is implemented and mapped in the Control Matrix with an owner and its evidence source.

gates.title: Validation complete
gates.description: The controls have been tested rather than merely built: findings recorded with remediations, detections written and shown to fire against the test, and evidence collection under way.

gates.title: Type I readiness / operating effectiveness
gates.description: Controls are tested, detections validated, metrics reported, an internal audit is complete, and the evidence packet is assembled — ready for the external Type I / Stage 1 auditor.

tasks.title: Kick-off & scope the engagement
tasks.objective: Sign the engagement paperwork and define exactly what the SOC 2 / ISO 27001 attestation covers.
learn: SOC 2 system description vs ISO 27001 Clause 4 scope

handoff.note: Red tests only what is in scope.

steps.title: Record the engagement agreement
steps.description: Capture the client, engagement type, and terms.
steps.instruction: Fill the Engagement Agreement & Scope form: client, engagement type (SOC 2 / ISO / combined), NDA, and sign-off.
steps.whatItMeans: This is the contractual and ethical anchor — like the Scope & RoE in a pentest, nothing proceeds until it is signed.

steps.title: Define the system / ISMS boundary
steps.description: Draw the exact boundary the attestation covers.
steps.instruction: In the same form, write the in-scope systems, data and locations, plus what is explicitly out of scope.
steps.whatItMeans: The boundary determines which controls apply, what Red may test, and what evidence the auditor samples. Too wide wastes effort; too narrow fails the audit.

tasks.title: Confirm rules of engagement
tasks.objective: Agree the testing targets, windows, and written authorization before any scanning.
prerequisites: GRC has recorded the engagement scope

steps.title: Confirm targets and authorization
steps.description: Cross-check the in-scope hosts and get written testing authorization.
steps.instruction: Read GRC’s engagement scope; confirm the exact hosts/URLs, allowed test windows, and that you have written authorization to test them.
steps.whatItMeans: Testing outside the authorized scope is illegal and voids the engagement — the PTES pre-engagement step exists to prevent exactly that.

tasks.title: Stand up logging & sensors
tasks.objective: Centralize logs and baseline “normal” so later detections and evidence have data to work with.
prerequisites: GRC has defined the system boundary
definitionOfDone: A baseline of normal activity captured

steps.title: Enable and centralize auditing
steps.description: Turn on host auditing and confirm logs flow.
steps.command: sudo systemctl enable --now auditd && sudo ausearch -m USER_LOGIN -ts today
steps.expectedOutput:
$ sudo ausearch -m USER_LOGIN -ts today
----
time->Mon Aug  5 09:12:44 2026
type=USER_LOGIN msg=audit(1754384: pid=1442 uid=0 auid=1000
 msg='op=login id=1000 exe="/usr/sbin/sshd" hostname=10.10.100.5
 res=success'

outputHighlights.label: a real audit record. Its presence proves auditd is not just running but actually recording — an active service with no events is a silent gap.
the outcome field. Auditing both success and failure is what SOC 2 CC7 and ISO A.8.15 expect — a failed-login record would read res=failed here.
what caused the event. Tying an event to the program behind it is the difference between a log and evidence an auditor will accept.

steps.whatItMeans: Central, tamper-evident logging is the foundation of SOC 2 CC7 monitoring and ISO A.8.15 — you cannot detect or evidence what you do not log.
steps.troubleshooting: No output → auditd may not be installed: `sudo apt install auditd`. On a container, use journald: `journalctl -u ssh --since today`.

tasks.title: Risk assessment & Statement of Applicability
tasks.objective: Assess the client against the frameworks and decide which controls apply (the SoA).
prerequisites: Engagement scope signed (Gate 1 depends on this)
definitionOfDone: ≥3 Annex A controls with applicability decisions

handoff.note: Blue implements the technical controls the SoA marks applicable.

steps.title: Assess risk and decide applicability
steps.description: For each Annex A control, decide whether it applies and why.
steps.instruction: Fill the Statement of Applicability form: add each Annex A control in scope, its applicability (Yes/No), the justification, and its status.
steps.whatItMeans: The SoA is the ISO 27001 centrepiece — the auditor reads it first to see what you claim and why. It also feeds the SOC 2 control set.

tasks.title: External attack-surface assessment
tasks.objective: Map the in-scope external attack surface to feed the gap analysis.
prerequisites: Rules of engagement confirmed
definitionOfDone: TLS/exposure issues noted for the gap analysis

handoff.note: GRC folds exposure gaps into the risk assessment.

steps.title: Scan the in-scope hosts
steps.description: Enumerate services on the authorized targets.

commands.explain: Service/version scan of one authorized host.

steps.expectedOutput:
Nmap scan report for 10.10.100.30
Host is up (0.00051s latency).

PORT    STATE SERVICE VERSION
22/tcp  open  ssh     OpenSSH 7.6p1 Ubuntu 4ubuntu0.7
443/tcp open  ssl/http nginx 1.14.0 (Ubuntu)
3389/tcp open ms-wbt-server Microsoft Terminal Services

Service detection performed. Nmap done: 1 IP address (1 host up)

outputHighlights.label: an old SSH version. In a gap assessment the exact version is the finding — it maps to specific advisories the client must patch.
RDP exposed to the network. Remote Desktop reachable externally is a classic high-risk gap that goes straight into the risk assessment.
you scanned exactly the one authorised host. Anything more would be outside the agreed scope and window.

steps.whatItMeans: A repeatable, authorized scan (NIST 800-115) is the credible basis for the “technical vulnerability” side of the gap assessment.
steps.troubleshooting: “Host seems down” → keep `-Pn`. No permission/blocked → confirm the host is in the authorized scope and window.

tasks.title: CIS baseline gap scan
tasks.objective: Measure current hardening against the CIS Benchmarks to find the control gaps.
prerequisites: Log centralization from Week 0 done
SSH / console access to the in-scope hosts
The relevant CIS Benchmark PDF to score against
definitionOfDone: Top hardening gaps recorded for Week 2

handoff.note: GRC references gaps when building the control matrix.

steps.title: Run a hardening audit
steps.description: Scan the host against a CIS-style baseline.
steps.expectedOutput:
[+] Results
  Warnings (1):
  ! SSH root login is permitted [SSH-7412]
  Suggestions (14):
  * Set a password on GRUB bootloader [BOOT-5122]
  * Disable core dumps for setuid programs [KRNL-5820]

  Hardening index : 58 [###########         ]

outputHighlights.label: the baseline score. Its whole value is the before/after pair — record it now so Week 2’s fixes have something to be measured against.
a warning, and warnings are your priority gaps. This one maps directly to SOC 2 CC6 access controls.
the test ID. Quoting it makes the gap traceable in the control matrix — an auditor can look up exactly what was checked.

steps.whatItMeans: Gaps against CIS map directly to SOC 2 CC6 and ISO A.8 controls, turning “harden the box” into auditable control work.
steps.troubleshooting: `lynis: command not found` → `sudo apt install lynis` (or run from a cloned copy).

tasks.title: Build the control matrix
tasks.objective: Map every control to its SOC 2 CC and ISO Annex A references, assign an owner, and name the evidence.
prerequisites: SoA complete (Gate 1)
definitionOfDone: ≥3 controls with SOC 2 or ISO references
Every control has an owner + evidence source

handoff.note: Blue implements and evidences the controls it owns.

steps.title: Map controls and assign owners
steps.description: Create the working crosswalk of controls.
steps.instruction: Fill the Control Matrix form: one row per control with its SOC 2 CC, ISO Annex A, owner, status, and the evidence an auditor would sample.
steps.whatItMeans: Build the control once and satisfy both frameworks — the matrix is how a multi-framework MSSP avoids doing the work twice.

tasks.title: Implement the technical controls
tasks.objective: Stand up the missing controls GRC assigned and record what changed.
prerequisites: Control Matrix assigns Blue’s controls
definitionOfDone: Each change recorded for the evidence trail

handoff.note: GRC updates the matrix status to Implemented/Operating with evidence.

steps.title: Enforce baseline access controls
steps.description: Apply a default-deny firewall and log the change.

commands.explain: Permit only the services you intend to expose.

steps.expectedOutput:
$ sudo ufw status verbose
Status: active
Default: deny (incoming), allow (outgoing), disabled (routed)

To         Action      From
--         ------      ----
22/tcp     ALLOW IN    Anywhere

outputHighlights.label: the control is actually enforcing. An "inactive" firewall with correct rules is a control that exists on paper but not in operation — the exact thing an auditor tests for.
the default-deny posture CC6.6 and ISO A.8.20 expect. Everything is blocked unless explicitly allowed below.
the one justified exception. A short, reasoned allow-list is the evidence — a long one undermines the default-deny claim.

steps.whatItMeans: This is a control implementation, not just a config — record it so it becomes sampled evidence in the matrix and packet.
steps.troubleshooting: Locked out of SSH? Always `ufw allow 22/tcp` BEFORE enabling. On a remote box, keep an open session while you test.

tasks.title: Threat-model the proposed controls
tasks.objective: Check the controls being implemented against the attack paths found in Week 1, and say which ones actually close them.
prerequisites: Attack-surface findings from Week 1
Control Matrix with owners assigned (in progress)
learn: Threat modelling against a control set
definitionOfDone: Every Week-1 finding mapped to the control that is meant to close it
Any finding with no control covering it raised to GRC before the gate

handoff.note: GRC records the uncovered findings in the matrix as gaps or accepted risks, with a reason.
Blue implements the controls that close a real finding first.

steps.title: Map each finding to the control that closes it
steps.description: Walk the Week-1 findings against the control matrix.
steps.instruction: Walk your Week-1 findings against the control matrix.
instructionList: For each finding, name the control in the matrix meant to close it.
Say how you would retest that finding once the control is in.
Where no control closes a finding, write it down and tell GRC.
steps.whatItMeans: An auditor asks whether a control addresses the risk it claims to. Checking that while the controls are still being built beats finding out in Week 4 that one closes nothing.

tasks.title: Penetration test & retest
tasks.objective: Test the implemented controls, then retest every fix to prove closure.
prerequisites: Controls implemented (Gate 2)
definitionOfDone: Every high/critical retested and recorded Closed/Open/Risk-accepted

handoff.note: Blue uses the attack timeline to validate detections.

steps.title: Test and record findings
steps.description: Run the authorized test against the in-scope app.
steps.instruction: Perform the authorized test; for each finding, record severity, remediation, and (after the fix) the retest result in the form.
steps.whatItMeans: A finding that is fixed and retested Closed is the strongest operating-effectiveness evidence for CC4.1 / A.8.8 — “we test, and the fixes hold”.

tasks.title: Detection engineering
tasks.objective: Write detections mapped to ATT&CK and validate them against the Red team’s activity.
prerequisites: Red is running the test (attack telemetry available)
definitionOfDone: ≥1 validated as Fired against Red’s test

handoff.note: GRC references validated detections as CC7 evidence.

steps.title: Write and validate detections
steps.description: Author detections for the attacks Red is running.
steps.instruction: For each attack technique, add a detection to the Detection Rules form — log source, ATT&CK id, logic — then mark whether it fired during Red’s test.
steps.whatItMeans: Detections that provably catch a real attack satisfy SOC 2 CC7.2/7.3 monitoring — not “we have a SIEM” but “our monitoring works”.

steps.title: Spot the attack in the logs
steps.description: Confirm the attack is visible in your log source.

outputHighlights.label: a classic injection probe in a URL. Real users never send this — a match is what proves your detection has genuine attack data to fire on, not a hypothetical.
the attacker’s IP during the test window. Record it and the timestamp — these become the metrics that show the detection actually caught Red’s activity.
a second, different technique. Two distinct payloads landing lets you map more than one ATT&CK id to real evidence.

steps.whatItMeans: Seeing the attack in the logs is the difference between a theoretical rule and a validated detection.
steps.troubleshooting: No matches → check the correct log path (`/var/log/nginx/access.log`) and that the test actually hit this host.

tasks.title: Coordinate validation & collect evidence
tasks.objective: Track remediation to closure and start collecting the evidence each control needs.
prerequisites: Retest results from Red (what closed, what remains)
Control Matrix with an owner and evidence named per control (Gate 2)
definitionOfDone: Evidence gathered for each implemented control

steps.title: Track remediation and gather evidence
steps.description: Update control status and collect the sampled artifacts.
steps.instruction: For each control in the matrix, move status toward Operating and collect the concrete evidence artifact (config, log, ticket, report).
steps.whatItMeans: Auditors sample evidence, not intentions — collecting it as you go turns Week 4 from a scramble into an assembly job.

tasks.title: Close out the retest and attest
tasks.objective: Finish the Retest & Validation report — every finding resolved one way or another — and attest to the result for the evidence packet.
prerequisites: Week-3 findings recorded with remediations
Fixes deployed by Blue
learn: Risk acceptance with a named owner
definitionOfDone: Every finding reads Closed, Open or Risk accepted — none left blank
The methodology section states how each retest was performed
Anything still Open or Risk accepted names who accepted it and why

handoff.note: GRC files it in the evidence packet as the operating-effectiveness evidence for CC4.1 / A.8.8.

steps.title: Resolve every finding and attest
steps.description: Retest what is still open, then attest to the result.
steps.instruction: Take the report from “tested” to “closed out”.
instructionList: Retest anything still open from Week 3 and set its result.
For each Open or Risk-accepted finding, record who accepted it and why.
Fill the methodology section: how the retests were done, not just that they were.
steps.whatItMeans: The auditor’s question is not “did you test?” but “what happened to what you found?”. A blank retest column is an open finding by default, and a risk accepted without a named owner is an omission, not an acceptance.

tasks.title: Report detection & response metrics
tasks.objective: Compute the MTTD/MTTR and coverage numbers a Type II auditor samples for CC7.
prerequisites: Detections deployed and validated against Red’s activity (Week 3)
Alert/incident timestamps available to compute MTTD/MTTR

steps.title: Report the response metrics
steps.description: Summarize detection/response performance over the window.
steps.instruction: Fill the Detection & Response Metrics form from your SIEM/IR tickets: incidents, MTTD, MTTR, coverage, false-positive rate.
steps.whatItMeans: Numbers over an observation window are what turns a Type I “designed” control into Type II “operating effectively”.

tasks.title: Run the internal audit
tasks.objective: Do the mandatory ISO 9.2 internal audit before the external auditor arrives.
prerequisites: Control Matrix + evidence collected
definitionOfDone: Every nonconformity has a corrective action

handoff.note: Fix nonconformities before assembling the packet.

steps.title: Audit your own controls
steps.description: Independently review each control against its evidence.
steps.instruction: Fill the Internal Audit Report form: for each control, record conformity / minor NC / major NC and a corrective action with an owner.
steps.whatItMeans: Finding and fixing your own nonconformities first is the whole point of the internal audit — it is far cheaper than the external auditor finding them.

tasks.title: Assemble the audit evidence packet
tasks.objective: Index every control to its evidence artifact so the external auditor can sample it.
prerequisites: Internal audit complete
All role deliverables in
definitionOfDone: Every item has an owner + location

steps.title: Index the evidence to controls
steps.description: Build the auditor’s index of evidence.
steps.instruction: Fill the Audit Evidence Packet form: one row per evidence artifact, tied to its SOC 2 CC / ISO Annex A control, with owner, type, location and period.
steps.whatItMeans: A control mapped to concrete evidence is a control an auditor can pass. This packet is the deliverable that gets the client through Type I / Stage 1.

steps.title: Export the engagement package
steps.instruction: On the Deliverables page, click Download team package to produce the zip of all eight engagement deliverables.
steps.whatItMeans: One clean package — agreement, SoA, control matrix, validation, detections, metrics, internal audit, evidence — is what you hand the auditor.

deliverables.title: Engagement Agreement & Scope
deliverables.purpose: Define the client, the system boundary, and the terms of the engagement — the equivalent of the SOC 2 “system description” scope and the ISO 27001 Clause 4 scope statement.
deliverables.howTo: Fill every field. The in-scope systems/data boundary drives every later control, test, and evidence item. Nothing is assessed until the agreement is signed off.

fields.label: System / ISMS boundary
fields.help: The systems, services, data and locations the attestation covers.
fields.placeholder: Production AWS account, the customer web app + API, the supporting CI/CD, the corporate identity provider.

dod.label: Client, system boundary and sign-off are filled in
Engagement type and start date are set

deliverables.title: Statement of Applicability (SoA)
deliverables.purpose: The centrepiece ISO 27001 document — for each Annex A control, state whether it applies, why, and its implementation status. The auditor reads this first.
deliverables.howTo: Add a row per Annex A control you are addressing. Justify inclusion/exclusion. “Status” tracks design → operation.
deliverables.source: Risk assessment (which controls treat which risks)

group.label: Annex A controls
group.help: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A has 93 controls across 4 themes (Organizational, People, Physical, Technological).

dod.label: At least three Annex A controls with an applicability decision
Every applicable control has a justification

deliverables.title: Control Matrix
deliverables.purpose: The working crosswalk — each control mapped to its SOC 2 Common Criteria and ISO Annex A references, with an owner, its implementation status, and the evidence that proves it operates.
deliverables.howTo: One row per control. “Evidence” names the artifact an auditor would sample (a config, a log, a ticket, a report).
deliverables.source: SoA + the hardening/detection work Blue implements

columns.label: Control
columns.placeholder: MFA enforced on all admin access

columns.label: Evidence
columns.placeholder: IdP MFA policy export + access review log

seed.evidence: IdP policy export + Q2 access review
SIEM rule pack + sample alert ticket

dod.label: At least three controls, each with a SOC 2 or ISO reference
Every control names an owner and evidence

deliverables.title: Retest & Remediation-Validation Report
deliverables.purpose: Prove the controls actually work: for each finding from the assessment, record the fix and the retest result. This is the “operating effectiveness” evidence a Type II / Stage 2 auditor wants.
deliverables.howTo: One row per finding. Retest each after remediation and record Closed / Open / Risk-accepted with the retest date.

fields.label: Methodology
fields.placeholder: PTES + OWASP WSTG; authenticated + unauthenticated; retest of every high/critical after remediation.

seed.remediation: Parameterised queries; WAF signature; input validation

dod.label: At least one finding with a retest result
Every critical/high finding has a remediation recorded

deliverables.title: Detection Rules
deliverables.purpose: The MDR detection content that satisfies SOC 2 CC7.2/CC7.3 (“monitoring for anomalies”) and ISO A.8.16 — each rule mapped to the ATT&CK technique it detects and validated against the Red team’s activity.
deliverables.howTo: One row per detection. Map to an ATT&CK technique and note whether it fired during the validation test.
deliverables.source: The Red team’s test activity (detections must catch it)

seed.name: SSH brute force
seed.logic: >10 failed logins / 1 min from one IP → alert

dod.label: At least two detections mapped to an ATT&CK technique
At least one detection validated as “Fired”

deliverables.title: Detection & Response Metrics
deliverables.purpose: Operating-effectiveness metrics for the monitoring & response controls — MTTD/MTTR and detection coverage over the observation window, the numbers a Type II auditor samples for CC7.
deliverables.howTo: Fill the metric fields from the SIEM/IR tickets over the observation window.

fields.label: Commentary / trend
fields.placeholder: MTTR down 30% after the IR runbook rollout; coverage gap on lateral-movement techniques.

dod.label: Observation window and coverage are set

deliverables.title: Internal Audit Report
deliverables.purpose: The mandatory ISO internal audit (Clause 9.2) run before the external auditor — find your own nonconformities and fix them first. Feeds the management review (9.3).
deliverables.howTo: Record findings against controls: conformity, minor or major nonconformity, with the corrective action and owner.

fields.label: Internal auditor
fields.placeholder: GRC lead (independent of the control owner)

fields.label: Audit scope
fields.placeholder: All applicable Annex A controls + SOC 2 CC1–CC9.

columns.label: Corrective action
columns.placeholder: Patch + tighten SLA; re-audit in 2 weeks

seed.finding: Two high findings open past the 30-day SLA
seed.action: Remediate + add SLA alerting; re-audit in 2 weeks

dod.label: At least one audit finding with a result and corrective action
Every nonconformity has a corrective action

deliverables.title: Audit Evidence Packet
deliverables.purpose: The index the auditor works from — every control mapped to the concrete evidence artifact, who owns it, and where it lives. Turns a pile of files into a defensible audit trail.
deliverables.howTo: One row per evidence item. Reference the control (SOC 2 CC / ISO Annex A) and the exact artifact + location.
deliverables.source: The Control Matrix + all role deliverables

seed.artifact: IdP MFA policy export + access review
SIEM rule pack + sample alert ticket

dod.label: At least three evidence items, each tied to a control
Every evidence item names an owner and location
